description: Drop Morgan bit columns that are set in fewer than 5% or more than 95% of the training molecules (mask computed on training features only and applied to the test features), leaving the random forest settings unchanged.

Append the RDKit 2D descriptor vector (Descriptors._descList, cached per SMILES) to the Morgan bits, with NaN/inf set to 0 and values clipped to the training-set 1st-99th percentiles, and keep the random forest unchanged.
Switch the Morgan fingerprint to radius 3 with 4096 bits, keeping the rest of the random forest pipeline (including the accepted descriptor features) unchanged.

Replace the random forest with a LightGBM L1 regressor on the same Morgan and descriptor features, choosing among 12 randomly sampled grid configurations by 4-fold GroupKFold on Murcko scaffolds, then refitting the best on all training data.

The job timed out because the inner LightGBM grid search (12 configs x 4 inner folds, plus a final fit, for each of the 15 outer fits, about 735 boosting runs of 600 rounds on roughly 2250 features) exceeds the 600 s limit, so I cut the search to a single config.
Add a 1024-bit feature-invariant (FCFP-style) Morgan fingerprint, concatenated with the 1024-bit ECFP fingerprint in place of the previous 2048-bit ECFP.

Add a sklearn MLPRegressor (512,128 ReLU, alpha 1e-3, early stopping, standardised target) on the Morgan fingerprint columns and average its predictions 50/50 with the LightGBM output; sklearn has no dropout, so the spec's dropout is omitted.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only changes LightGBM hyperparameters and the search grid (more rounds, a lower learning rate, bagging, L2 regularisation, feature_fraction fixed at 0.2). It adds no file or network access, no pasted values and no use of test labels.

No bugs that would make the result meaningless. The grid still yields (nl, mcs, ff) tuples in the shape lgb_params expects. The seed is still passed through. Runtime should stay similar, since the grid has 9 configs instead of 18 and each runs 1000 rounds instead of 600.

Recomputed z = (0.5585 - 0.555) / (0.0042 * sqrt(2)) ≈ 0.59, using an sd of 0.0042 per run and one run on each side. This matches the reported 0.601 within the rounding of the shown values. The gain of 0.0035 is smaller than one run's noise, so rejecting is reasonable. A replicate would be needed to support any claim of improvement.

description: Switch the LightGBM regressor to the spec's subsampled setup: bagging 0.6 every round, feature_fraction fixed at 0.2, lambda_l2 5.0, learning rate 0.02 and 1000 rounds, with the inner grid trimmed to num_leaves and min_child_samples.

Skip the Crippen logP/TPSA block: those six physchem columns (MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds) are already in the full RDKit descriptor vector that train.py feeds LightGBM, and the spec's random forest no longer exists in the script.

Append 9 hand-written ionisable-group SMARTS counts (carboxylic acid, tetrazole, acyl sulfonamide, primary/secondary/tertiary aliphatic amine, amidine/guanidine, quaternary N, phenol) as integer columns to the Morgan fingerprint features.

Stack three base learners (random forest, LightGBM L1 with fixed config, Tanimoto kernel ridge on ECFP bits) using scaffold-grouped 5-fold out-of-fold predictions, and blend them with a non-negative Ridge meta-learner.

Replace the random forest base learner with a CatBoostRegressor (MAE loss, 1000 iterations, depth 6, lr 0.05, l2 3) on the same ECFP+FCFP+descriptor features, with border_count=64 added to bound runtime.

Replace the random forest base learner with a CatBoostRegressor (MAE loss, 1000 iterations, depth 6, lr 0.05, l2 3) on the same ECFP+FCFP+descriptor features, with border_count=64 added to bound runtime.
Lower the stack's random forest to max_features=0.2 and impute NaN/inf descriptor values with the training-column median instead of zero.
Early-stop the stack's LightGBM L1 member on a 10% scaffold-grouped inner validation split (up to 2000 rounds, patience 100), then refit on all data with 1.1x the best iteration count.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted answers. Test labels are never used: the scaffold groups come only from train_smiles, and the early-stopping validation split is drawn only from the training rows (Xa).

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The diff changes the method in two ways. First, LightGBM now stops early on a 10% split grouped by Murcko scaffold and is then refit on all rows for 1.1 times the best iteration count. Second, the out-of-fold stacking with a positive Ridge meta-model is removed, and the three base predictions are now averaged with equal weights.
My guess at why the loss got worse: dropping the learned stacking weights probably accounts for most of it, since a plain mean gives equal weight to a weaker base learner.

Recomputed z: the difference is 0.5826 − 0.5357 = 0.0469. The standard error is 0.0042 × √(1/1 + 1/1) ≈ 0.00594, so z ≈ −7.90, which matches the harness's −7.904. The candidate is much worse, so reject is correct.
Only one run each for the candidate and the incumbent, but a 0.047 gap is far beyond the noise, so the conclusion holds.

description: The job timed out because the 5-fold inner stacking loop repeated all three base learners (RF, LightGBM with early stopping plus refit, and Tanimoto KRR) six times per fit; I replaced the stacking with a plain average of the three base predictions, cutting base-learner fits per job by about 6x.
Add an SVR with a precomputed Tanimoto kernel (C=5, epsilon=0.1) as a fourth base learner in the stack, reusing the same ECFP Tanimoto Gram matrix as the existing kernel ridge member.
Add an SVR with a precomputed Tanimoto kernel (C=5, epsilon=0.1) as a fourth base learner in the stack, reusing the same ECFP Tanimoto Gram matrix as the existing kernel ridge member.

Replace the stack's random forest base learner with a LightGBM regressor using the L1 objective (800 trees, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 31, min_child_samples 10, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging 0.8 every round), keeping the same Morgan and descriptor features.

Replace the stack's random forest base learner with a LightGBM regressor using the L1 objective (800 trees, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 31, min_child_samples 10, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging 0.8 every round), keeping the same Morgan and descriptor features.

Add six 3D shape descriptors (PBF, NPR1, NPR2, radius of gyration, inertial shape factor, eccentricity) from one ETKDGv3 conformer per molecule, cached per SMILES, clipped to the training 1st-99th percentiles, and appended to the tree-model input only (fixed embedding seed 42 so the per-SMILES cache is seed-independent).
Replace the stack's Tanimoto kernel learner with a standalone KernelRidge tuned over alpha in [0.01, 0.1, 1.0] by inner 5-fold CV.
Append the 167-bit MACCS key fingerprint to the Morgan (ECFP + FCFP) feature block in featurize, leaving the random forest settings and the ECFP-only Tanimoto kernel unchanged.

issues: Recomputed z: (0.5357 - 0.5062) / (sqrt(2) * 0.0042) = 0.0295 / 0.00594 ≈ 4.97. This matches the harness value of 4.969, apart from rounding.

I found no file or network access, no pasted answers and no use of test labels. The kernel uses only the training rows (Fa, Za, ya) for the solve, and the standardisation mean and sd come from Za only.

The diff does not show where the descriptor columns are clipped. The comment says they were 'already clipped to 1st-99th percentiles on the full train set'. If those percentiles are computed in fit_predict from the training rows only, it is fine. If they also use test_smiles, that is mild transductive use of test inputs, not their labels. That would not change the result much, but it should be checked.

The diff does not show that X really has 2*N_BITS fingerprint columns followed by descriptor columns. If the offset were wrong, the result would still be valid but the RBF kernel would not use the intended features.
The diff makes two changes at once: it adds the RBF kernel on descriptors and lowers the ridge term from 1.0 to 0.5. We cannot tell how much of the gain comes from each.
Each side has only one run. A gain of about 5 sd is large, but one replicate run would make the result firmer. It does not block acceptance.

description: Make the stack's kernel ridge member use a summed Tanimoto (ECFP) plus RBF kernel on z-scored RDKit descriptors, with lambda 0.5 and gamma 1/(2 n_descriptors), leaving the other base learners and the Ridge meta-learner unchanged.
Abort: sweeping min_samples_leaf x max_features with 500-tree forests would multiply the random forest cost and likely exceed the 10-minute job limit.

Append an atom-pair count fingerprint (1024 bits) and a topological-torsion count fingerprint (512 bits) to the Morgan ECFP+FCFP block, and move the descriptor slice in base_predict to a fixed offset so the new columns don't break it.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted answers. Test SMILES are only featurized, and their labels are never used. Clipping percentiles come from Dtr (the training fold) only.

The RBF descriptor slice [2*N_BITS : 2*N_BITS+len(_descList)] is correct only if X is laid out as [Morgan bits (2*N_BITS) | descriptors | BRICS]. The old comment and code suggest it is, but featurize and the hstack are not shown in the diff, so I could not confirm this.

Effectiveness concern, not a bug: the BRICS hashed counts go through the same 1st-99th percentile clipping as the descriptors. Most of the 512 sparse bins are nonzero in fewer than 1% of molecules, so their 99th percentile is 0. Clipping then sets those columns to 0 and throws away most of the BRICS signal. Consider excluding the BRICS block from clipping.

Speed and cosmetics: BRICS decomposition is not cached, so it runs again on every one of the 15 fits. That is probably fine within 10 minutes for 3360 molecules, but caching it like desc_vector would be cleaner. The comment in brics_counts repeats the docstring note of _frag_hash. BRICSDecompose would crash on an unparseable SMILES (MolFromSmiles returns None), but the benchmark SMILES should all parse, as the existing descriptor code already assumes.
No harness numbers yet, so z cannot be computed and there are no claims to check against results.

description: Append a 512-bucket count vector of BRICS fragments (deterministic zlib.crc32 hashing, clipped like the descriptors) to the tree-model feature matrix only, keeping the RBF kernel on descriptors and the Tanimoto kernel on ECFP bits.
Abort: averaging RF and LightGBM alone would discard the kernel-ridge stack member, and the existing positive Ridge meta-learner already covers any weighted average of RF and LightGBM.

Replace the stack's random forest base learner with xgboost.XGBRegressor (pseudo-Huber loss, huber_slope 0.5, depth 6, 600 rounds, subsample 0.8, colsample 0.3, min_child_weight 3, seeded), keeping the LightGBM and kernel members and the stacking unchanged.

Replace the bit-vector ECFP and FCFP Morgan fingerprints with count fingerprints (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy, radius 2, 1024 bits per block as in the incumbent), leaving the forest, LightGBM, kernel and stacking settings unchanged.

Weight the random forest and LightGBM members by 1/sqrt(1+density), where density is the count of other training-fold molecules with ECFP Tanimoto >= 0.5, normalised to mean 1, leaving the kernel ridge member unweighted.

issues: No integrity problems: the new kernel ridge tuning (9 settings, 4-fold inner split with molecules grouped by scaffold) uses only training-fold data. groups[tr] or the training groups are passed, and no test labels are used.
mu appears to be computed from all of ya before the inner split, so the mean of the training labels leaks into the tuning folds. The effect is negligible and no test data is involved.
Recomputed z = (0.5062-0.4895)/(sqrt(2)*0.0042) = 0.0167/0.00594 ≈ 2.81, which matches the harness's 2.815. Dividing by the single-run sd instead gives 3.98.
Each side has only one run. The gain is large compared with the noise, but a replicate would confirm it if budget allows.

Runtime cost: 36 extra matrix solves of about 2000x2000 per base_predict call, roughly 3,000 extra per job. Check the job time against the 10-minute limit before adding more. One eigendecomposition per inner fold, reused for every lam value, would be cheaper.
The tuning grid includes the old settings (lam=0.5, wr=1.0), and test-time prediction uses the same kernel blend as the training solve. No bug found.

description: Grid-search the kernel ridge lambda (0.1, 0.5, 2.0) and RBF weight (0.5, 1.0, 2.0) with a 4-fold scaffold-grouped inner CV inside base_predict, then refit the kernel ridge member on all rows with the best pair.

Make the LightGBM base learner a residual model: an inner scaffold-grouped 5-fold out-of-fold Tanimoto kernel ridge prediction is added as a feature, LightGBM L1 fits y minus that prediction, and the test output is the kernel ridge prediction plus the LightGBM residual.

The job timed out because each base_predict call ran a 9-config KRR grid search (36 dense solves) and was repeated about 90 times across the 15 fits, so I removed the grid search, halved the random forest size, and shortened LightGBM training.

Fit all three base learners and the kernel member on the residual of a one-variable least-squares line in Crippen MolLogP (fit on each training fold), then add the baseline back so the meta-learner still sees raw-scale predictions.

Replace the kernel ridge member's single ECFP Tanimoto kernel with the average of ECFP radius 1, ECFP radius 2 and count-based atom-pair min/sum Tanimoto kernels (divided by 3), keeping the RBF term and the lambda/RBF-weight grid.

The job timed out because each fit_predict runs base_predict six times (five stacking folds plus the final fit), and each call re-runs a 9-configuration by 4-fold kernel ridge grid search (36 dense solves on about 2200 samples). The fix removes that inner grid search and uses the fixed setting lam=0.5, wr=1.0, which was the default and a central grid value.

Add a fourth base learner to base_predict: an ElasticNet (alpha=0.01, l1_ratio=0.5, max_iter=5000) fit on the z-scored descriptor columns concatenated with the ECFP and FCFP bits, whose prediction joins the out-of-fold matrix so the Ridge meta-learner blends it with the other three.

The crash is a width mismatch: base_predict returns four base-learner columns (RF, LightGBM, KRR, ElasticNet) but the out-of-fold array was allocated with three, so I changed the allocation to four columns.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only changes LightGBM hyperparameters: it switches to DART boosting (drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, max_drop=50) and lowers N_ROUNDS from 600 to 400. It adds no file access, no pasted answers and no use of test labels.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. One caveat: LightGBM's DART does not work properly with early stopping or best_iteration. If the unchanged code around this diff uses early stopping or a validation split to pick the number of rounds, the DART runs would be using the wrong round count. That would make the comparison less fair, but it would not make the result invalid.
Two things change at once: the boosting type and the number of rounds. Even if the candidate had won, the gain could not be credited to either change alone.

The numbers support the reject. The candidate scores 0.4914 against the incumbent's 0.4895, which is 0.0019 worse. Recomputing with noise sd 0.0042 and one run each gives z = (0.4895 - 0.4914) / (0.0042 * sqrt(2)) ≈ -0.32. The harness's -0.315 differs only by rounding of the 4-decimal values.
The candidate is only 0.3 sd worse, so this is not evidence that DART is worse. It is just no evidence of improvement. DART also costs more compute per round.

description: Switch the stack's LightGBM L1 base learner to DART boosting (drop_rate 0.1, skip_drop 0.5, max_drop 50) with 400 rounds, keeping the other LightGBM settings, the seed, and the rest of the stack and Ridge meta-learner unchanged.
Smooth the stack's test predictions with 20 steps of label propagation over a kNN (k=10) Tanimoto graph built on the union of training and test ECFP bits, clamping training rows to their true labels.

Add a second kernel-ridge stack member using the product kernel K = Tanimoto(ECFP) * RBF(standardised descriptors), with its lambda chosen from the same grid by the existing inner grouped CV, and feed it to the meta-learner as a fourth column alongside the unchanged sum-kernel member.

Train the LightGBM base learner in two stages: 400 rounds of Huber (delta = median absolute deviation of the training targets), then 300 more rounds continued from that model with regression_l1 at learning rate 0.01, keeping leaves 31, min_child_samples 10 and feature_fraction 0.2.

The crash happens because the LightGBM Dataset is built with default free_raw_data=True, so it is freed after the first lgb.train and cannot be reused when continuing training with init_model; setting free_raw_data=False on that Dataset fixes it.
